title: Antibiotic use and resistance in livestock
bottleneck: Livestock consume the majority of the world's antibiotics, much of it for growth promotion and prophylaxis in crowded conditions, accelerating antimicrobial resistance that kills over a million people yearly. Alternatives — vaccines, probiotics, better husbandry — exist but cost more or demand management skills industrial systems aren't built for; bans in one region shift production to unregulated ones. Bans in one region shift production to unregulated ones, and alternatives cost more or demand skills industrial systems lack.
why_it_blocks: AMR is a slow pandemic, and animal agriculture is its largest driver. Failing to decouple protein production from antibiotics endangers modern medicine.
current_state: The EU banned growth-promotion antibiotics; global livestock use keeps rising, concentrated in regions with weak oversight.
